slides.title:
Enzyme storage:
a 14-day screen
slides.subtitle:
Which formulation merits confirmation at 4 C?
Synthetic pilot; no validated shelf-life claim.
slides.notes: All observations, formulations, lots, and thresholds are invented for presentation testing. No empirical or clinical claim is made. The title page should remain a quiet report opener, not a product reveal.

slides.title: The lot, not the well, is the replicate
slides.subtitle: Synthetic paired design: three lots split across all conditions

table.caption: SYN-L1. Technical duplicates are averaged before each lot-level ratio. Assay uses initial rate in U/mL; 1 U converts 1 micromol/min under the assumed assay conditions.

slides.notes: Each lot has its own day-0 denominator under each formulation. The duplicate wells do not increase the number of independent biological lots. All concentration definitions are nominal formulation concentrations.

slides.title: Glycerol clears the screening threshold
slides.subtitle: Mean day-14 residual activity at 4 C; synthetic n = 3 lots per condition
slides.caption: SYN-L1. Equal-weight means of three lot ratios. Lot ranges: buffer 58-66%, glycerol 88-94%, trehalose 80-88%. No error bars, confidence interval, or significance claim; individual lots follow.
slides.notes: Bar axis begins at zero. The 85% cutoff is a screening convention chosen for this invented exercise. Higher residual activity does not establish formulation compatibility or a shelf-life specification.

slides.title: All three glycerol lots exceed 85%
slides.subtitle: Synthetic paired ratios expose the spread hidden by the means

table.caption: SYN-L1. Every value is day 14 divided by its matched formulation-specific day 0, multiplied by 100. Three lots cannot characterize manufacturing variability.

slides.notes: The exact raw rates and duplicate wells are retained in synthetic_data.json. A 3/3 screening pass is not a statistical guarantee for future lots.

slides.title: Retention is not assay compatibility
slides.subtitle: Synthetic screen separates a storage signal from a deployable formulation

left.title: What the screen supports
bullets: Three of three lots exceed the chosen 85% threshold.
Advance one candidate to a confirmation study.

right.title: What remains unmeasured
bullets: Matrix effects after dilution into the final assay.
Viscosity, recovery, contamination, and freeze-thaw tolerance.
Potency beyond 14 days or at other temperatures.

slides.verdict: Synthetic candidate selection only; no formulation release or shelf-life assignment.
slides.notes: These missing measurements are limitations, not invented adverse results. Preserve all three unmeasured categories in visible slide copy.

slides.title: Confirmation must earn the next claim
slides.subtitle: Proposed synthetic study sequence; no work has been performed

milestones.label: 01 / matrix
milestones.title: Check compatibility
milestones.body: Compare fresh formulations at the final assay dilution; verify blanks and spike recovery.

milestones.label: 02 / storage
milestones.title: Expand the window
milestones.body: Six new paired lots at days 0, 7, 14, and 28; keep the day-0 denominator per lot.

milestones.label: 03 / decision
milestones.title: Set criteria first
milestones.body: Predeclare retention and precision limits before results; investigate any failed lot.

slides.caption: SYN-L2. Proposed design only. Six lots are a planning choice, not a power calculation; no minimum validated shelf life follows from this proposal.
slides.notes: This is a true sequential study plan, not decorative pacing. All three stages remain editable milestone objects.

slides.title: Advance glycerol; withhold shelf life
slides.subtitle: Synthetic conclusion for an assay-development meeting
bullets: Advance 5% v/v glycerol to a compatibility-first confirmation study.
Keep the evidence unit at the lot; report all failures and raw rates.
Do not authorize production release, clinical use, or a shelf-life label.
slides.summary_callout: A promising 14-day screen is a reason to test, not a validated storage instruction.
sources: SYN-L1/L2 | all facts and plans invented
